knowledge:
- key_parameters: bam=Vector of paths to BAM files for the replicates ;; chrN=Chromosome name to analyze (e.g., "chr2") ;; chrL=Chromosome length (e.g., 1e6) ;; idr=Irreproducible Discovery Rate threshold (default 0.01) ;; N=Number of top peaks to use for IDR (e.g., 3e4) ;; p=p-value threshold for peak-pair calling (default 1e-12) ;; EXT=Extension size in bp for plotting (e.g., 500)
- alternatives: ChIP-seq peak callers (mentioned generally, but cexor is preferred for ChIP-exo data because it models strand-specificity and base-pair resolution using the Skellam distribution)
- when_to_use: When analyzing ChIP-exo replicate datasets to identify high-resolution protein-DNA binding events and centers using strand-specific peak-pair modeling and reproducibility assessment.
- pitfalls: Using a too-stringent p-value threshold during peak-pair calling can prevent proper IDR estimation because the noise component is excluded; peak-pair calling should be relaxed (e.g., p-value=1e-3) to allow separation into reproducible and irreproducible groups. IDR calculation results can vary depending on the choice of initial estimates for the four parameters (mu, sigma, rho, prop); trying several choices is recommended to avoid local maxima.

workflows.name: chip_exo_peak_calling
workflows.intent: Call reproducible peak-pairs and identify protein-DNA binding events and centers from ChIP-exo replicate BAM files, followed by visualization.
workflows.stages: 1. Load the CexoR package and locate BAM files ;; 2. Call reproducible peak-pairs using the cexor function ;; 3. Extract reproducible binding events and centers ;; 4. Plot the mean profile of lambda exonuclease stop sites and reads using plotcexor
workflows.code:
library(CexoR)
rep1 <- "CTCF_rep1_chr2_1-1e6.bam"
rep2 <- "CTCF_rep2_chr2_1-1e6.bam"
rep3 <- "CTCF_rep3_chr2_1-1e6.bam"
r1 <- system.file("extdata", rep1, package="CexoR",mustWork = TRUE)
r2 <- system.file("extdata", rep2, package="CexoR",mustWork = TRUE)
r3 <- system.file("extdata", rep3, package="CexoR",mustWork = TRUE)
peak_pairs <- cexor(bam=c(r1,r2,r3), chrN="chr2", chrL=1e6, idr=0.01, N=3e4, p=1e-12)
peak_pairs$bindingEvents
peak_pairs$bindingCentres
plotcexor(bam=c(r1,r2,r3), peaks=peak_pairs, EXT=500)
